item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed local government public officers about workplace corruption risks and reporting.
item.support:
The survey 
focused on perceptions about workplace vulnerability to corruption, personal 
experiences of corruption, and reporting.

item.text: The Commission cautioned that the voluntary responses reflected perceptions and might not represent the whole local government workforce.
item.support:
As such, the responses might not 
represent the perceptions of all local government public officers.

item.text: The Commission reported that participants perceived nepotism and favouritism in recruitment and career opportunities as the leading corruption risks.
item.support:
Nepotism and favouritism in recruitment, promotions and other 
career opportunities were perceived to be the most prevalent corruption risks.

item.text: The Commission recommended targeted training, secondary employment policies, closer monitoring of contract outcomes and safer reporting arrangements.
item.support:
It is 
recommended that local councils ensure that they develop and implement policies 
relating to secondary employment.

item.quote:
The potential risks associated with secondary employment need to be better 
identified and managed.

There is a need for further training and education concerning corruption risks that 
are specific to someone’s role.
